level.title: A2 Elementary Punjabi
goals: Navigate routine travel and shopping conversations politely.
Describe health, completed actions, and everyday experiences.
Make plans and invitations using clear future forms.

lessons.title: Travel and Directions
lessons.learn: Learn to ask where places are, understand simple route instructions, and use respectful Punjabi while travelling. Read each Gurmukhi sentence with its romanisation, then notice the postpositions that describe movement and location.

grammar.title: Giving route instructions
grammar.explain: Punjabi commonly uses an imperative verb after the direction. Use ਜਾਓ (jao) for a polite instruction to one person or a group. Location words often come before ਹੈ (hai).

examples.en: The station is far from here.

mistakes: Do not use the intimate command ਜਾ (ja) with a stranger; choose polite ਜਾਓ (jao).

dialogue.t: ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰਨਾ, ਬੱਸ ਅੱਡਾ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹੈ?

dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the bus station?

dialogue.t: ਨਹੀਂ, ਇਹ ਬੈਂਕ ਦੇ ਨੇੜੇ ਹੈ।
dialogue.r: nahin, ih bank de nere hai.
dialogue.en: No, it is near the bank.

lessons.title: Tickets and Transport
lessons.learn: Practise buying a ticket, asking about departure time, and stating a destination. Punjabi often marks the destination with ਨੂੰ (nun) and uses polite request forms in service encounters.

grammar.title: Polite requests with ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ
grammar.explain: To request a countable feminine item such as ਟਿਕਟ (tikat), use ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ (chahidi hai). Add destination + ਨੂੰ (nun) to say where you need to go.
grammar.pattern: person + ਨੂੰ (nun) + item + ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ (chahidi hai)

examples.t: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਦੀ ਇੱਕ ਟਿਕਟ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।
examples.r: mainun amritsar di ikk tikat chahidi hai.
examples.en: I need one ticket to Amritsar.
The bus will leave at nine o’clock.

mistakes: Match ਚਾਹੀਦਾ/ਚਾਹੀਦੀ/ਚਾਹੀਦੇ (chahida/chahidi/chahide) with the requested noun, not with the speaker.

dialogue.t: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਲੁਧਿਆਣੇ ਦੀ ਟਿਕਟ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।
dialogue.r: mainun ludhiane di tikat chahidi hai.
dialogue.en: I need a ticket to Ludhiana.

dialogue.t: ਇੱਕ ਪਾਸੇ ਦੀ ਜਾਂ ਵਾਪਸੀ ਦੀ?
dialogue.r: ikk pase di jaan vapasi di?

dialogue.en: Return. How much is the fare?

lessons.title: Shopping and Prices
lessons.learn: Handle a simple market conversation: ask the price, choose a quantity, compare items, and bargain politely. Numbers and measure words come before the noun in Punjabi.

grammar.title: Comparing with ਨਾਲੋਂ
grammar.explain: Place the item used as the comparison before ਨਾਲੋਂ (nalon), meaning “than.” The adjective agrees with the thing being described.

examples.t: ਲਾਲ ਕਮੀਜ਼ ਨੀਲੀ ਕਮੀਜ਼ ਨਾਲੋਂ ਮਹਿੰਗੀ ਹੈ।
examples.r: lal kamiz nili kamiz nalon mahngi hai.
examples.en: The red shirt is more expensive than the blue shirt.

mistakes: Do not translate English “more cheap”; Punjabi uses the adjective with ਨਾਲੋਂ (nalon).

dialogue.t: ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਅੰਬਾਂ ਦੀ ਕੀਮਤ ਕੀ ਹੈ?

dialogue.en: What is the price of these mangoes?

lessons.title: Health and Advice
lessons.learn: Describe common symptoms and understand basic advice. Use ਨੂੰ (nun) with the person experiencing a condition, and practise ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ (chahida hai) for gentle recommendations.

grammar.title: Giving advice with ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ
grammar.explain: Use a verb stem plus ਣਾ and ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ (na chahida hai) to say what someone should do. The experiencer can be marked with ਨੂੰ (nun).
grammar.pattern: person + ਨੂੰ (nun) + infinitive + ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ (chahida hai)

examples.t: ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਣੀ ਪੀਣਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ।
examples.r: us nun pani pina chahida hai.
examples.en: He or she should drink water.

examples.t: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਡਾਕਟਰ ਕੋਲ ਜਾਣਾ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ।
examples.r: mainun daktar kol jana chahida hai.
examples.en: I should go to the doctor.

mistakes: Do not use the bare imperative when giving gentle medical advice; infinitive + ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ is softer.

dialogue.en: I have a fever and a cough.

dialogue.en: Take this medicine twice a day.

lessons.title: Past Activities
lessons.learn: Talk about completed everyday actions using the simple past. Punjabi past forms can agree with the object when a completed transitive action uses ਨੇ (ne), so learn complete sentence patterns rather than isolated endings.

grammar.title: Completed past actions
grammar.explain: With many completed transitive verbs, mark the doer with ਨੇ (ne). The perfective verb often agrees with an unmarked object. Intransitive verbs such as ਜਾਣਾ (jana) usually have no ਨੇ.

examples.en: I went to the market yesterday.

mistakes: Do not add ਨੇ (ne) automatically to every past sentence; common intransitive verbs normally omit it.

lessons.title: Plans and Invitations
lessons.learn: Make near-future plans, invite someone, accept or decline politely, and state a time. Punjabi future verbs show person, number, and often gender; this lesson gives useful whole forms for everyday planning.

grammar.title: Future plans
grammar.explain: Future forms attach to the verb stem and agree with the subject. Common forms include ਮੈਂ ਜਾਵਾਂਗਾ/ਜਾਵਾਂਗੀ (main javanga/javangi) and ਅਸੀਂ ਜਾਵਾਂਗੇ (asin javange).

examples.en: I will come in the evening.

mistakes: Choose a future ending that matches the subject; do not use ਆਵਾਂਗਾ (avanga) for every speaker.

dialogue.en: We will celebrate a birthday on Saturday.

dialogue.t: ਸ਼ਾਮ ਨੂੰ ਛੇ ਵਜੇ। ਕੀ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਆਓਗੇ?
dialogue.r: sham nun chhe vajje. ki tusin aoge?
dialogue.en: At six in the evening. Will you come?
